This petition is filed by the Petitioner against Respondent No.1 to 3 under Sec.166 of M.V.Act 1989 for the relief of compensation.

2. The brief facts of the case is as under; That on 15.08.2022 at about 7.15 a.m. he was working as loader and unloader of the lorry bearing Reg.No.NL01AF6813 near Doddahalla, Doddaballa Bengaluru District, at that time, driver of the said lorry driver the same in high speed in rash and negligent manner and dashed against the electric pole, as a result lorry was toppled, due to tremendous impact, petitioner fell down and sustained grievous injuries.

Immediately after the accident, he was taken to Prolife Hospital, Bengaluru, after firstaid he was shifted to ESIC Hospital,
Bengaluru for further treatment, for which he has spent SCCH5 an amount of Rs.15,00,000/
towards medical expenses and other incidental expenses.
3. At the time of the accident he was aged about 47 years, hale and healthy, working as loader and unloader, thereby earning Rs.25,000/ p.m.,

due to the accidental injuries sustained by him, he is not able to continue his work and is under complete bed rest, as such incurring from loss of income and he is suffering from permanent disability.
Out of this accident crime No.21/2022 is registered against the driver of the lorry bearing Reg.No.NL01AF6813 before the Hosahalli Police for the offences punishable under Sec.279, 337 of IPC.
R1 is the owner, R2 is insurer, R3 is present R.C.Owner of the said lorry, they are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation.

Hence, prays to allow the SCCH5 petition and grant compensation of Rs.15,00,000/ with interest at the rate of Chakala Venkatesulu Alias Venkatesulu vs Sri Bala Murali Transort on 14 August, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/84145414/
2 12% p.a.

sentences.text: On service of notice, Respondent No.1 and 3/owners have remained absent, hence placed exparte.
Respondent No.2/insurer has appeared and filed his written statement and denied the averments of the petition.

He has stated that, petition is liable to be dismissed for miss joinder of necessary parties as such the vehicle involved in the alleged accident occurred on 15.08.2022 from the vehicle bearing Reg.No.NL01AF 6813, but the policy number mentioned in the petition pertains to Goods carrying vehicle bearing Reg.No.TN23 CD6548 and same was in force from 17.01.2022 to 16.01.2023, but in the police records the vehicle which caused the accident is mentioned as NL01 AF6813 and no policy was issued to the same as on the date of SCCH5 accident.
Further denied age, occupation and income of the petitioner.
Claim made by the petitioner is higher, hence his petition is not maintainable.
Accordingly prays to dismiss the petition.

5. On going through the rival pleadings of the parties, my learned predecessor has framed the following:
::ISSUES::
1.

Whether Petitioner proves that, on 15.08.2022 at about 7.15 a.m. when the petitioner was a loader and unloader of the Lorry bearing Reg.No.NL01AF6813 was proceeding near Doddahalla, Doddaballapura Hosahalli Road, Bengaluru District, at the time the driver of the said lorry drove in a very high speed in a rash and negligent manner and dashed against the Electric pole and lorry was topple due to which the petitioner fell down and sustained grievous injuries, as mentioned in claim petition?
SCCH5 2. Whether the Petitioner is entitled for compensation as prayed in the petition?

If so from which respondent?
3. What order or award?

6. In order to prove his case, petitioner himself deposed his evidence as PW1, examined Dr.Ramesh as PW2, Medical Record Assistant at ESI Hospital as PW3 and marked 21 documents as per Ex.P.1 to Ex.P.21 and closed his evidence.

On the other hand, Manager of R2 is examined as RW1 and marked 2 documents as per Ex.R.1 and Ex.R.2 and closed his evidence.
7.

Heard the arguments and perused the evidence available on record, then my findings on the above issues are as follows:
Issue No.1 : In the Affirmative Issue No.2 : Partly in the Affirmative SCCH5 Issue No.3 : As per final order for the following:

Under such circumstances, considering the said evidence and believing the evidence of the petitioner, this tribunal comes to the conclusion that, petitioner has proved the above issue No.1 in his favour.
Accordingly I have answered above Issue No.1 in the affirmative.
14. Issue No.2:
As per the evidence of the petitioner, he had sustained left subtrochanteric fracture of femur.

In this regard he has furnished copy of wound certificate marked as Ex.P.5, discharge summary marked as Ex.P.11 issued by ESIC Model Hospital, Rajajinagar, SCCH5 Bengaluru wherein he took treatment as indoor patient since 15.08.2022 to 30.08.2022.

Further Dr.Ramesh, Orthopaedic Surgeon at Victoria Hospital, Bengaluru is examined as PW2 and he has exhibited OPD Book marked as Ex.P.15, Xray Films marked as Ex.P.16.
PW2 has assessed permanent physical disability of 34% of left lower limb, which is 17% of the whole body.
In crossexamination of PW1, he has admitted one or two points, but they have not support the case of the respondents.

16. On perusal of the evidence of PW1, PW2 and records i.e., exhibits marked corroborates the case of the petitioner that, out of the accident as alleged in the petition and evidence of PW1 and as per Ex.P.5 wound certificate, he has sustained abrasion on the anterior aspect of left leg, abrasion on the anterior aspect of the SCCH5 right knee, which are simple in nature and he has also sustained fracture shaft of left femur, fracture upper shaft of left femur, which are grievous in nature.
17.
Further Dr.Ramesh, Orthopaedic Surgeon at Victoria Hospital, Bengaluru is examined as PW2 and he has exhibited OPD Book marked as Ex.P.15 and Xray Films marked as Ex.P.16.
PW2 has assessed the permanent physical disability of 34% of left lower limb, which is 17% of the whole body.
In crossexamination he has categorically admitted that, he has not treated the petitioner.
Further he has deposed that, as per the case sheet at the time of the discharge the condition of the patient was stable and now the fractures are united and implants are in situ.

So considering the nature of the injuries sustained by the petitioner, functional disability SCCH5 is assessed at the rate of 10%
for the purpose of calculation of loss of future income.

To substantiate the SCCH5 said fact, he has not placed any documentary evidence.
In the absence of documentary evidence, I have no hesitation to disbelieve the case of the petitioner on the fact about occupation is concerned.

Under such circumstances, with reference to the year of accident, relying upon the guidelines issued by Hon'ble Karnataka State Legal Services Authority Bengaluru, notional income of the petitioner is taken at the rate of Rs.14,750/ p.m. so that, said fact is taken into consideration for the purpose of calculation of loss income during laid up period and also for the purpose of calculation of loss of future income.

Accordingly I hold that, the Petitioner is entitled for total compensation of Rs.3,00,396/ with interest at the rate of 6% p.a. from the date of petition till its realization of entire amount.

26. In the case on hand, respondent No.2 being the insurer has issued insurance policy bearing No.01628778370000 which is valid for the period from 17.01.2022 to 16.01.2023, the alleged accident was occurred on 15.08.2022 it reveals that, as on the date of accident, insurance policy was in force, but in written statement R2 has denied issuance of insurance policy in favour of R1 in respect of vehicle bearing Reg.No.NL01 AF6813 and the said policy is issued in respect of goods carrying vehicle bearing Reg.No.TN23CD6548.As SCCH5 discussed in issue No.1, naturally liability of respondent No.1 shall go against R2, so that, R2/insurer is directed to deposit the award amount with interest at the rate of 6% p.a. within 60 days from the date of this order.
With these views, I have answered Issue No.2 partly in the affirmative.
27. Issue No.3:

For the reasons assigned to Issues No.1 and 2, I proceed to pass the following:
::ORDER

The petition filed by the Petitioner under Sec.166 of the M.V. Act, 1989 is partly allowed with cost.
The Petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.3,00,396/ (Rupees Three Lakhs Three Hundred Ninety Six only) with interest at the rate of 6% p.a. from the date of petition till its realization.
